 Order

This miscellaneous appeal has been filed by the appellant/Insurance company under Section 173(1)
of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 , being aggrieved by the Award dated 24/01/2019 passed by VI Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District- Guna (M.P.) (in short "the Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No. 80/2015 whereby Claims Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.
7,70,000/- alongwith interest in favour of claimants.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District- Guna (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company submits that at the time of the accident,
the deceased Manoj was driving a goods vehicle bearing registration No. MP-06-E-5850 while holding a driving licence for Light Motor Vehicle (LMV) only, without any endorsement authorizing him to drive a transport/goods vehicle.
It is contended that the same constitutes a breach of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
On this ground, the appellant seeks setting aside of the impugned award and prays for exoneration from liability.
3. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent Nos. 1 and 2/claimants opposed the prayer and prayed for dismissal of the appeal.
Heard the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

sentences.text: It is not in dispute that at the time of the accident, the deceased Manoj was holding a valid LMV driving licence.
It is further evident from the record that the gross vehicle weight of the offending vehicle was 4020 kgs, which is less than 7,500 kgs.

6. In this regard, reliance can be placed upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mukund Dewangan vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. , AIR 2017 SC 3668, wherein the Apex Court has held as under:
"(ii) A transport vehicle and omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of either of which does not exceed 7,500 kg, would be a light motor vehicle and also motor car or tractor or a road roller, the 'unladen weight' of which does not exceed 7,500 kg; and the holder of a driving licence to drive the class of 'light motor vehicle' as provided in Section 10(2)(d) is competent to drive a transport vehicle or omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of which does not exceed 7,500 kg."

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. , AIR 2017 SC 3668
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan (supra) , this Court does not find any substance on merits.
Accordingly, no interference is warranted in the impugned award passed by the Claims Tribunal.
8. In view of the foregoing discussion, the instant miscellaneous appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.
